messages:
Erin M: FYI - escalating for ACME's on-prem HSM after last week's deploy. Customers started seeing signing failures and retries. Error surfaced as HSM_ERR_AUTH and intermittent timeouts. Impacting prod traffic and billing complaints.

Sanjay K: Can you paste a minimal repro and the relevant logs? Is this isolated to ACME or seeing across other tenants?

Erin M: Single customer for now (ACME Prod). Repro steps:
1) POST /v2/sign with key_id=acme-prod-01
2) Response 502 with body: "sign failed: HSM_ERR_AUTH"
3) Our client SDK auto-retries x3 -> customer reports 4x billed attempts

Lisa T: Pasting sanitized logs from their gateway: 
```
2026-03-16T18:22:10Z ERROR sign request id=abcd123 client=acme code=HSM_ERR_AUTH session=0x7f4
2026-03-16T18:22:10Z WARN hsm: rpc timeout after 5000ms
2026-03-16T18:22:11Z INFO retrying sign attempt=2
```

Matthew (oncall): Quick q — are they running an on-prem appliance or CloudHSM? If on-prem, which vendor/firmware? Also, please run and share: `sudo journalctl -u hsmd -n 200`, `pkcs11-tool --list-slots`, and `pkcs11-tool --test -k` on the HSM host.

Erin M: On-prem, vendor: SafeCrypt v3.2. Customer said firmware updated last week.

Lisa T: pkcs11-tool output (sanitized):
```
Slots: 1
Slot 0 - SafeCrypt v3 token present
C_CreateObject: CKR_OK
C_SignInit: CKR_DEVICE_ERROR
```

sec-bot: Alert: abnormal number of failed sign operations for key acme-prod-01 in last 1h (count=183, baseline=2). Possible key availability issue.

Sanjay K: CKR_DEVICE_ERROR during C_SignInit usually means the HSM returned an internal device error — could be queue exhaustion, firmware bug, or an auth/session leak. Two paths: (A) escalate to the vendor for hardware/firmware check; (B) short-term mitigation: failover to a hosted key variant or a secondary HSM if customer allows.

Erin M: Customer has strict key custody requirements — they will not allow keys to be exported. They asked us to engage SafeCrypt immediately. They also need audit logs for compliance; can we show retention and what events we capture?

Matthew (oncall): Audit logs: hsmd writes tamper/auth/audit events to /var/log/hsm/audit.log and optionally forwards to a remote syslog collector if configured. Default retention in their install is 30d. I can pull the last 48h bundle and upload. Also check `dmesg` for PCI issues and `strace -p <hsmd_pid>` if vendor asks for a trace.

Lisa T: Audit excerpt shows repeated `SESSION_AUTH_FAILED` followed by `DEVICE_OVERLOAD` events and then a flurry of `C_SignInit` failures.

Sanjay K: Actionable next steps: collect full hsmd logs, pkcs11 traces, firmware version, network topology (management/control plane), and whether a maintenance/reboot happened post-upgrade. I'll draft the vendor packet for SafeCrypt support.

Erin M: Also a billing issue: customer claims the retries caused 4x attempts charged between 18:20-18:40. They want a credit if this is our fault.

Lisa T: Looping in Billing: @billing-team — can we provisionally credit extra retries pending incident confirmation?

Billing Bot: Received request 987654. Billing will review after incident confirmation from Support/Eng.

Matthew (oncall): Uploaded logs bundle: https://redwood-secure-storage/incident/1779005123/logs.tar.gz — contains hsmd logs, pkcs11 outputs, audit excerpts.

Sanjay K: Opened SR with SafeCrypt: SR-99212. Vendor initial reply: "We've seen a queueing bug in SafeCrypt v3.2.1 under high concurrent sign load; patch v3.2.2 addresses it. We request a maintenance window for a rolling firmware update or an appliance reboot."

Erin M: Customer will not permit a full appliance reboot. Can we failover their signing route to a Redwood-hosted key proxy for 24h as a stopgap? Need legal/ops approval and explicit customer opt-in because of key custody policy.

sec-bot: Policy note: rotating to hosted keys requires explicit written customer consent due to custody/compliance constraints. Cannot auto-switch.

Lisa T: I'll draft the opt-in consent message outlining the tradeoffs (temporary hosted key, audit trail, rollback plan). Erin — want me to send to the customer and CC Legal?

Erin M: Yes, please. Also include a note that if vendor patch is applied and verified we will revert to on-prem keys.

Sanjay K: Vendor says patch is low-risk but needs a brief outage on the control plane — recommending canary on NonProd first.

Erin M: Good. Owners/ETA: Matthew — full log & pkcs11 trace (ETA 30m). Sanjay — vendor packet & SR (ETA 1h). Lisa — audit bundle + consent draft (ETA 45m). Billing — hold on credits until incident confirmed. Sec — monitor and block any auto-rotation.

Billing Bot: Noted. Billing will await incident closure for credit decisions.

Erin M: Thanks, team. Marking P1 and will update in 45m.

Matthew (oncall): Updating — vendor confirms patch 3.2.2 mitigates queueing. They can provide a hotfix with no key export but may need a control-plane restart on the appliance.

Erin M: Customer still declines any restart. Lisa — once consent text is ready I will send it and ask for explicit approval for hosted fallback.

Lisa T: Consent draft ready, sending to Erin now.

Erin M: Closing the loop for now. Will update after customer decision. Thanks.
